sources.entry: dlt - A Python library for building data pipelines with automatic schema inference, incremental loading, and support for multiple sources and destinations.

summary.one_liner: dlt is an open-source Python library that loads data from APIs, databases, files and DataFrames into typed, schema-inferred datasets across 20+ destinations.
summary.what_it_does: The library lets you describe REST API endpoints declaratively, or wrap any Python generator, iterable, pandas/Polars/Arrow object, SQL database, or cloud bucket of CSV/JSONL/Parquet files as a source. A pipeline then extracts, normalizes and loads the data, inferring schema and column types and creating tables in the destination. It supports incremental loading and merge (upsert) write dispositions via decorators, schema contracts with evolve/freeze/discard modes, and secrets/config injection. Destinations named in the README include DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Postgres, Redshift, Databricks, Athena, ClickHouse, MotherDuck and filesystem buckets. Loaded data can be read back via dlt.attach and a Dataset API returning DataFrames, Arrow tables or Ibis expressions. The README also mentions a dltHub managed platform and an optional "hub" extra, but the core library is pip-installable on its own.
use_cases: load REST API data into a warehouse
ingest CSV or Parquet files from S3, GCS or Azure
sync a SQL database into an analytics store
incremental or upsert loading of changing records
load pandas or Polars DataFrames into a database
prototype a data pipeline in a notebook with DuckDB
how_to_run: Define a @dlt.resource generator or rest_api_source config
notable: Declarative REST API source with pagination, filtering and mapping at extraction time
Schema inference, typing and ALTER TABLE schema drift handling
Schema contracts with evolve, freeze and discard modes
Dataset API to read loaded tables back as DataFrame, Arrow or Ibis expression
Designed as a library rather than a platform, usable in notebooks, Lambda, Airflow or laptops
caveats: Some optional extras are not yet available for Python 3.14, so that version is experimental
Managed deployment and extra features (transformations, data quality, observability) are part of the separate dltHub offering
